title: 1984 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In the obtuse triangle \(ABC,\) \(AM=MB,\) \(MD\perp BC,\) \(EC\perp BC.\) If the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(24,\) then the area of \(\triangle BED\) is

solutions.text:
Draw \(MC.\) Since \(EC\parallel MD,\) points \(E\) and \(C\) have equal perpendicular distances from \(MD,\) so \([DME]=[DMC].\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} [BED]&=[BMD]+[DME]\\ &=[BMD]+[DMC]\\ &=[BMC]. \end{aligned} \] Because \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB,\) triangle \(BMC\) has half the area of \(ABC.\) Thus \([BED]=12.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Draw segment \(MC\) and compare \(\triangle DMC\) with \(\triangle DME\)
Those triangles have the same base \(MD\) and equal altitudes; also \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\)
